tasks.title: Create agents/audit-planner.md — the recon specialist agent prompt
tasks.description: Create the audit agent prompt file at `agents/audit-planner.md`. This is a read-only recon specialist that does a cold sweep of a codebase through two cognitive lenses: security (adversarial) and SOLID/structural. The prompt must instruct the agent to: (1) read briefing materials (CLAUDE.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md, tasks.completed.json, prior planning-notes.md) for project context and to avoid re-flagging fixed issues, (2) perform two separate passes — security lens ("how do I abuse this?") and SOLID lens ("what will hurt to change in six months?"), (3) use confirm-then-remediate framing (every finding names specific files/functions, bounded confirmation locations, and remediation direction), (4) demote unbounded findings to investigation items (spike demotion), (5) return structured findings in the specified format: Codebase Overview, Security Findings, SOLID/Structural Findings, Reviewed and Judged Sound, Unresolved. The agent must NOT write planning-notes.md or know about its format — it returns raw findings. Use generalized module/component/directory language, not service-oriented language. Follow the pattern of existing agents in `agents/` (e.g., `planner.md`, `post-task-reviewer.md`).
tasks.notes:
# Task #1 Completion Notes

## What was done
Created `agents/audit-planner.md` — a read-only recon specialist agent prompt that performs cold codebase audits through two cognitive lenses:

1. **Security Pass** ("How do I abuse this?") — adversarial analysis of trust boundaries, injection surfaces, secret handling, file operations, child process spawning, and permission checks.

2. **SOLID/Structural Pass** ("What will hurt to change in six months?") — maintainability analysis of responsibility separation, hidden coupling, interface contracts, duplication, oversized modules, and missing extension points.

## Key design decisions
- **Confirm-then-remediate framing**: Every finding must name specific files/functions, provide bounded confirmation steps, and suggest a remediation direction. Unbounded findings are demoted to Investigation Items (spikes).
- **Read-only**: The agent does NOT write planning-notes.md or modify any project files — it returns raw structured findings.
- **Generalized language**: Uses module/component/directory/function, not service-oriented language.
- **Prior-work awareness**: Reads tasks.completed.json and planning-notes.md to avoid re-flagging fixed issues or rehashing settled decisions.
- **Follows existing agent pattern**: Same structure as planner.md and post-task-reviewer.md — briefing materials section, workflow steps, output format, and rules.

## Output format sections
- Codebase Overview, Security Findings (S-N), SOLID/Structural Findings (D-N), Investigation Items (I-N), Reviewed and Judged Sound, Unresolved

## Test changes
- Updated `test/commands/init.test.ts` line 1078: added assertion that `audit-planner.md` is installed by `installAgents()`.
- Full suite: 660 pass, 0 fail.

tasks.title: Create commands/codebase-audit.md — the slash command wrapper
tasks.description: Create the slash command at `commands/codebase-audit.md`, following the pattern established by `commands/generate-tasks.md`. This slash command instructs the planner agent to: (1) spawn the `audit-planner` agent via the Agent tool, (2) receive the structured findings report, (3) present a concise summary to the user organized by severity and lens — not the full raw output, but a digestible overview, (4) invite the user to discuss ("anything surprising? anything you know is already handled? anything to add?"), (5) when the conversation feels complete, write `planning-notes.md` incorporating the audit findings into the standard format (Context, Goals, Approach, Rejected Alternatives, Rough Task Outline, Open Questions). The user must be able to course-correct before anything gets generated. Reference `commands/generate-tasks.md` for structural patterns (how the slash command wraps a subagent invocation).

tasks.title: Verify ralph init installs new files + add tests
tasks.description: Verify that `installSlashCommands()` and `installAgents()` in `src/commands/init.ts` will automatically pick up the new `commands/codebase-audit.md` and `agents/audit-planner.md` files without any code changes. Both functions glob `*.md` from their respective source directories (`commands/` and `agents/`), so this should be automatic. Write a test in `test/commands/init.test.ts` that explicitly verifies: (1) when a `commands/` source directory contains `codebase-audit.md`, `installSlashCommands()` copies it to the target project's `.claude/commands/codebase-audit.md`, and (2) when an `agents/` source directory contains `audit-planner.md`, `installAgents()` copies it to the target project's `.claude/agents/audit-planner.md`. Use temp directories as mock ralph roots (following the existing test pattern with `ralphRoot` parameter overrides). The test should confirm the files are present with correct content after installation.

tasks.title: Investigate --allowedTools and the Agent tool
tasks.description: The planner is spawned with `--allowedTools Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit` (in `src/commands/plan.ts` line 162). The `/generate-tasks` and `/codebase-audit` slash commands instruct the planner to use the `Agent` tool, which is not in that allowlist. The open question is whether `--allowedTools` restricts the `Agent` tool or whether `Agent` is always available. Investigate this by: (1) reading the Claude CLI documentation or help output (`claude --help`, `claude man` or similar) to understand `--allowedTools` behavior with respect to the Agent tool, (2) if `Agent` IS restricted by `--allowedTools`, add `Agent` to the allowlist in `src/commands/plan.ts` (change the `--allowedTools` value from `'Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit'` to `'Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit,Agent'`), (3) if `Agent` is NOT restricted (i.e., it's always available regardless of `--allowedTools`), document this finding in the task notes and leave the code unchanged. This affects both the existing `/generate-tasks` command and the new `/codebase-audit` command.

tasks.title: End-to-end verification — build, test, and smoke test
tasks.description: Final verification that everything works together. Steps: (1) Run `bun test` and confirm all tests pass (existing + new from task 3). (2) Run `bun run build` and confirm the compiled binary builds successfully. (3) Verify the new files exist at their expected paths: `agents/audit-planner.md` and `commands/codebase-audit.md`. (4) Verify the agent prompt contains the key structural elements: two-lens separation (security + SOLID), confirm-then-remediate framing, spike demotion, bounded confirmation, structured findings format, project context reading instructions. (5) Verify the slash command references the `audit-planner` agent by name and includes instructions for the planner to spawn it, present findings, continue conversation, and write planning-notes.md. (6) Run `ralph init` in a temp directory (or verify via the test suite) that both new files get installed to `.claude/commands/` and `.claude/agents/`. Document all results in task notes.
